abstract: Finite-height Collatz words are feasible on intervals of mechanical phase, so summing phase-box counts duplicates words. We prove that the average multiplicity, weighted by the exact source-cylinder densities, is bounded independently of word length. At each phase boundary a legal clipping of the defect path sends every word in the new box to a newly entering word. A finite weighted partition sum controls each fiber, including the change in terminal cylinder modulus. For slope $3/2\le\lambda<5/3$, the overlap constants are $4$ at height one and $15$ at height two. Multiplying by the largest circular gap $G_b$ of the rotation gives an upper bound $C_kG_b$ for the cylinder-weighted average feasible phase span. We also prove the existence of a phase cell of length at least $\tau/(b+1)$ whose aggregate defect-box density is at most $(C_k+k)/(1-\tau)$ times its length times the full-language density. These estimates apply to the actual bounded-height language without a probabilistic conditioning transfer. In canonical cycle coordinates they reduce the interval-length term in a necessary integer count; on the existing record pair its effective length is below $0.062$ of the common state cap at height one and $0.23$ at height two. The additive one-per-word term remains, and the explicit bound still excludes neither class. We specify the additional translation-moment inequality needed for a selected-cell application, without asserting it. Exact checks use one unchanged 38-word fixture and a fixed rational scalar calculation. No new cycle exclusion or solution of the conjecture is claimed.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: Bounded weighted phase overlap for finite-height Collatz words
